📌 Tehran, IRNA –The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) says the passage of maritime vessels through the Strait of Hormuz is currently not possible, blaming the disruption of transit on illegal US military activities in the region.

The authority, which is mandated to authorize and regulate maritime transit through the waterway linking the Persian Gulf to the Sea of Oman, made the announcement in a message posted on its X social media network on Sunday.
​
“We hereby inform all esteemed applicants: Due to the recent illegal movements of the United States’ military forces in the region, passage through the Strait of Hormuz is currently not possible,” the post said.
​
Noting that the website PGSA.ir is the only channel for obtaining transit permits, the message further stated that once stability and calm are restored in the strait, all requests will be reviewed according to the schedule to issue the necessary permits for ships.
​
The PGSA operates a mandatory online clearance system for all vessels intending to transit the Strait of Hormuz, a mechanism that has gradually increased the number of ships safely navigating the authority's designated routes.
​
Nevertheless, the US military continues to interfere with shipping in the strait and surrounding waters, violating the Islamabad memorandum of understanding and disregarding calls that foreign powers have no role in the strategic waterway.
